key_insight: Among the detonation-sprayed WC coatings tested, WC–Co–Cr delivered the best combined hardness, friction, scratch resistance, and corrosion performance.
engineering_relevance: WC–Co–Cr coatings show promise for extending the service life of pipeline valves and other oil-and-gas components exposed to wear and corrosion.
method: Deposited WC coatings with Co–Cr, Ni, and NiCr binders by detonation spraying.
Characterized microstructure and elemental distribution using SEM and EDS mapping.
Evaluated microhardness, tribology, scratch resistance, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: WC–Co–Cr achieved 1232.55 HV microhardness and a 0.515 friction coefficient, with the best reported corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt.% NaCl; porosity was lowest for WC–Ni (0.40%) and highest for WC–NiCr (2.78%).
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term field durability under combined wear, corrosion, and service loading.
paper_title: Impact Of Co–Cr, Ni, and NiCr binder systems on the microstructure and functional properties of WC coatings produced by detonation spraying
